objections.text: The pull's alias filter is minimisation, not permission: any member reads any item of the server (the shared entries, every member's workspace entries, any project's items). A person who does not want their workspace knowledge read by the team keeps the workspace root off (part 4's roots). The ADR says it; the Sharing page already says a shared item reaches the team.

The first admin's code is printed to the container's log and stays there until the log rotates. It is single-use and expires in 24 hours; the runbook says to rotate the first admin's token after joining and how to rotate Docker's logs.
Withdrawn text stays in entry_revisions and in the mirror's history until purged, and a tombstone keeps a memory's bytes. serve purge is the erasure path (D-24) and the ADR says when to use it.
Any member may push a new revision of any shared or project entry (D-12). A vandalised entry is rolled back by an admin's reinstate of an earlier revision, and the last writer is recorded.

Memories hold personal data (a developer's titles and bodies name people and projects): the server stores them verbatim for a project set to Knowledge and memories, redaction is the client's edge, and the server refuses recognisable secrets only. The ADR names the boundary, as part 4's did.
A waiting pull is one open connection per device; at the team's scale it is nothing, and a proxy with a short response timeout would cut it (Caddy's default has none). The runbook names it.
